label: Tech, data & AI
tagline: The strongest fit for an AI-assisted competitor
intro: Machine-learning and data competitions are the one group where an AI agent can do most of the work: the task is published, the metric is objective and the submission is scored automatically. Prize money is real but concentrated at the top of the leaderboard, and the work is measured in weeks, not minutes.

label: Forecasting
tagline: Small prizes, low effort, many open tournaments
intro: Metaculus runs rolling forecasting tournaments with cash pools and states plainly that participation is free. Pools range from a few thousand dollars to $50,000, and some listed tournaments explicitly carry no prize pool. Effort per question is minutes, so this is the cheapest place to start.

label: Creative & writing
tagline: Free entry exists, but many contests charge fees
intro: Several of the best-known writing and photography prizes are free to enter and pay cash; others charge an entry fee, and a few are restricted by geography or by rules that ban AI-generated work. Read the fee line first, then the AI line.

label: Fantasy & pick'em
short: Sports picks, survivor and fantasy games
tagline: Free entry is normal here; prizes are modest
intro: US media pick'em games are free by rule and pay fixed weekly and season prizes. Most are season-long commitments with a handful of minutes of work each week. Outside the US the picture changes: many fantasy games pay merchandise or tickets rather than cash.

label: Market simulations
tagline: Read the prize paragraph before the rules
intro: Broker demo contests are usually free and run on virtual money, but many pay 'trading bonuses' credited to a live account rather than withdrawable cash. One broker on this list states that plainly; treat every other demo contest the same way until its own terms say otherwise.

label: Skill games
tagline: Mostly paid entry, not a free cash path
intro: The large mobile skill platforms fund their cash prizes from entry fees and take a platform cut. Their free rooms pay in-app currency. A handful of free tournaments exist on esports and gaming platforms, but the advertised prize is often bonus credit.

label: Trivia & rewards
tagline: Cash is rare and often crowdfunded
intro: Trivia and reward apps often advertise large totals that are crowdfunded over time or paid in points. Givling, the largest name in this group, now describes itself as a crowdfunding competition, not a fixed prize pool.

label: Pool tools
short: Software for office and survivor pools
tagline: Not contests - other people fund the prizes
intro: These are tools for running a pool you and your friends fund, not competitions an operator pays out. They are kept here so they are not mistaken for free prize money.

label: Directories
tagline: Start here to find new contests
intro: Directories do not run contests; they index other people's. They are the fastest way to find a new opportunity, and the worst way to confirm a prize, because their listings lag the organisers' rules.
